SELECTED_INDEX: 3  
CONFIDENCE: 0.33  
EXPLANATION: The experimental spectrum shows:  
• A strong carbonyl stretch at 1712 cm⁻¹ – typical for a saturated aliphatic ketone (~1715 cm⁻¹, rule GFQ-011).  
• Intense CH₂/CH₃ stretches at 2884–2939 cm⁻¹ and a CH₂ scissoring band at 1454 cm⁻¹ – indicating a chain with several methylene groups (rule GFQ-003).  
• Two C–C skeletal bands at 1120 and 1040 cm⁻¹ that are characteristic of long, all-trans aliphatic chains.  

Among the candidates, only 3, 4 and 7 contain a carbonyl (C=O).  
– Candidates 1, 6, 8 are esters; their C=O Raman band would appear higher (~1735 cm⁻¹).  
– Candidate 7 is highly branched and has few CH₂ groups, inconsistent with the strong CH₂ features observed.  
– Candidate 4 (hexan-3-one) has a shorter chain, giving weaker trans-chain skeletal bands.

Candidate 3 (CCCC(=O)CCC, heptan-4-one) is a straight-chain, mid-chain ketone whose expected Raman bands match the 1712 cm⁻¹ C=O, strong CH₂ features at 1454 cm⁻¹, and the 1120/1040 cm⁻¹ C–C stretches. It best fits the observed pattern.
